newsitem.title: USA: Vivra says its dialysis records subpoenaed.
newsitem.headline: Vivra says its dialysis records subpoenaed.

text.p: Vivra Inc said Friday that it has been subpoenaed by a federal grand jury to show records of the operations of Vivra Renal Care.
The subpoena was from the United States Attorney for the District of Massachusetts.
The company said the subpoena concerns its previous relationship with Damon Clinical Laboratories, and blood tests billed to Medicare and Medicaid.

In a press release, the company said the subpoena "appears to focus on Vivra's previous relationship with Damon Clinical Laboratories and other affiliated entities, as well as utilization patterns and procedures pertaining to clinical laboratory blood tests billed to the Medicare and/or Medicaid programs."
Vivra said it has been advised that Vivra Renal Care is now a subject of the United States Attorney's investigation. Vivra said it will cooperate fully.

The company said the government is seeking documents from January 1, 1987, through July 1, 1996, that pertain to kidney dialysis facilities owned, managed or operated by Vivra and its affiliates, as well as all agreements and communications with Damon.
